origin: Original deterministic Python synthesis. No samples, recordings, model output, network source or commercial game audio.
scope: Source-only listening candidates. Nothing in this directory is wired to the game runtime, audio graph, HUD, simulation or build.

revision.description: Whole batch regenerated with the same recipe, seeds and sample counts, then multiplied by -3 dB. Only amplitude changes; the final peak stays at or below the -12 dBFS ceiling.

priorityIntent.status: Future integration intent only; this batch has no runtime consumer.
priorityIntent.policy: Gunfire and threat cues keep priority. The four candidates play in a lower UI/round tier and must not duck, delay, replace or schedule around combat audio. If a cue cannot be heard without masking combat, skip the cue instead of raising it.
priorityIntent.mixOwnership: Runtime mix levels remain open. This batch only fixes file peak at or below -12 dBFS.
priorityIntent.concurrency: At most one instance per cue event; a repeat of the same ID replaces the previous instance.

cues.character: Low-energy short mechanical latch: a filtered click, a small low body and one quieter spring tick. No tonal weapon report and no two-tone motif.

event.trigger: Authoritative switch acceptance, not keydown. Do not play on key repeat, on a rejected command, when the requested weapon already matches, or per rendered frame.

cues.character: Single soft pulse: one attack and one decay, no second click and no ascending/descending pair.

event.condition: Play once per confirmed primary menu action, only after settings.canPlay() allows it.
event.trigger: Unique trigger point: the start/next/restart onclick handlers in src/ui/hud.ts:22, training route src/candidates/offline-training-v1/ui/hud.ts:23. The resume(), next() and restart() functions in src/client.ts and src/candidates/offline-training-v1/client.ts are downstream handlers, not additional hook points. The training next() calls resume() at its end, and once match.summary.complete it calls restart() instead (src/candidates/offline-training-v1/client.ts:62); hooking next(), resume() or restart() separately would play the cue more than once per action. Do not play on hover, focus, menu open/close, a rejected settings draft, range input, or every UI click.

bindings.role: Unique trigger point (main route): onclick runs only after settings.canPlay() returns true.
Downstream handler only, not a hook point. Called by start and again at the end of next(); at most one cue per confirmed action.
Downstream handler only, not a hook point. Calls resume() at its end, so hooking next() and resume() would double the cue.
Downstream handler only, not a hook point. Does not call resume().

Downstream handler only, not a hook point. Usually calls resume() at its end; once match.summary.complete it calls restart() instead (line 62), so hooking next(), resume() or restart() would play the cue more than once per action.
Downstream handler only, not a hook point. Does not call resume(); also reached from next() when match.summary.complete (line 62), so it must not add its own cue.
